newsitem.title: TURKEY: February frost seen negligible for Turk grain crop.
newsitem.headline: February frost seen negligible for Turk grain crop.

text.p: Turkish traders and producers said on Monday the effect of the February frost on the grain crop in southern and central regions was negligible and the harvest outcome depended more on spring rains.
"Crop loss due to the frost may be around only two to three percent," said a Turkish-based international trader.
He told Reuters overall crop losses due to frost could be balanced by a larger wheat area in southern regions.
"We do not think this is a problem for Turkey's overall grain production," he said.
Crop estimates would not be known before a field survey to be carried out by the government in May.
Local government officials in southern regions, where the frost had a much bigger impact, said losses occurred mainly in citrus groves and greenhouses.

"Citrus producers and vegetable greenhouses were caught off-guard by the frost last month. No one expected temperatures of 11-12 degrees (Celsius) below zero at that time of year," said one official from Adana province.
Officials said most losses were among lemon trees. Frost hit 3,300 hectares of citrus and 6,500 hectares of wheat in the region.
